pitch:
# A minesweeper game

## 1. People and their journey
**Player** (the only role). Arrives at a fresh board, sees the mine counter, timer and grid, and decides which cell to reveal or flag. Plays until every safe cell is revealed (win) or a mine is revealed (loss), then chooses to start a new game or change difficulty.

## 2. How it looks
The product looks like classic Windows Minesweeper: a grey beveled window with a raised panel holding a counter, a face button and a timer above a sunken grid of square tiles.

- **Page background**: flat mid-grey (#c0c0c0) filling the view, with the game window centred on it.
- **Game window**: raised grey frame with a light-white top-left bevel and dark-grey bottom-right bevel, holding the difficulty bar, header panel and board.
- **Difficulty bar**: a row at the top of the window with three choices: Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. The current one is shown with a sunken button.
- **Header panel**: sunken-bordered grey strip across the top of the window, holding the mine counter, face button and timer.
- **Mine counter**: left of the header; black rectangle with three red seven-segment digits showing mines minus flags. It goes negative (for example -02) when flags exceed mines.
- **Face button**: centre of the header; raised square, yellow round face. Smiling normally; shocked "o" mouth while a tile is held down; sunglasses after a win; dead "x" eyes after a loss. Sunken while pressed.
- **Timer**: right of the header; black rectangle with three red seven-segment digits counting seconds, capped at 999. Stops on win or loss.
- **Board**: sunken-bordered grid of square tiles below the header, with no gaps between tiles.
- **Hidden tile**: raised grey square with white top-left and dark-grey bottom-right bevels. Looks flat-sunken while held down by the pointer.
- **Revealed tile**: flat light-grey square with a thin darker-grey outline, showing a number or nothing.
- **Number colours**: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, 4 dark blue, 5 maroon, 6 teal, 7 black, 8 grey. A zero shows blank.
- **Flagged tile**: hidden-style raised tile with a red flag on a black base.
- **Mine (on loss)**: revealed tile with a black spiky mine. Unflagged mines are shown on loss.
- **Exploded mine**: the mine tile the player clicked, with a red background.
- **Wrong flag (on loss)**: a flagged tile that was not a mine shows the mine with a red cross over it.
- **Win display**: when the game is won, all unflagged mines automatically get flags and the counter shows 000.

## 3. How it is used
- **Click a hidden tile** (tap on touch): reveals it. The first reveal starts the timer.
- **Click a number tile** whose adjacent flag count equals its number (chord): reveals all its other unflagged hidden neighbours.
- **Right-click a hidden tile** (long press on touch): places a flag; on a flagged tile it removes the flag.
- **Press and hold on a tile**: the face turns shocked until release.
- **Click the face button**: starts a new game with the same difficulty.
- **Click a difficulty choice**: starts a new game at that size.
- **Click a flagged tile**: nothing happens.
- **Click any tile after the game ends**: nothing happens.

## 4. Scope
One loop: choose a difficulty, reveal and flag tiles, finish with a win or loss, then restart. Beginner is 9×9 with 10 mines, Intermediate is 16×16 with 40, and Expert is 30×16 with 99. There is no custom size, no saved games and no sound.

## 5. Things and their states
- **Game**: holds difficulty, board, elapsed seconds and flag count. States: ready (no reveal yet), in progress, won, lost. The first reveal moves it from ready to in progress; revealing a mine moves it to lost; revealing every safe tile moves it to won. The face button or a difficulty choice starts a new game in the ready state.
- **Tile**: holds a mine flag and an adjacent-mine count (0–8). States: hidden, flagged, revealed. Reveal moves hidden to revealed, and the flag action toggles hidden and flagged.

## 6. Rules
- Mines are placed at the first reveal, never on the clicked tile, so the first click is never a mine.
- The first click's neighbours are also kept mine-free, so the first reveal opens an area.
- A tile's count is the number of mines among its up to 8 neighbours.
- Revealing a mine ends the game as lost.
- Revealing a zero tile automatically reveals all its neighbours, repeating through further zeros.
- Cascades never reveal flagged tiles, and the cascade stops at numbered tiles.
- Revealing a flagged tile is refused and nothing changes.
- Flags can only be placed on hidden tiles; flagging a revealed tile is ignored.
- Flags may exceed the mine count; the counter goes negative.
- A chord on a number whose adjacent flags do not match is ignored.
- A chord reveals neighbours, so a wrong flag can cause a loss on a mine.
- A chord on a hidden or revealed zero tile does nothing.
- The game is won when all non-mine tiles are revealed; flags are not required.
- The timer starts on the first reveal, ticks once a second and stops on win or loss.
- Flagging before the first reveal is allowed and does not start the timer.
- After a win or loss, reveals, flags and chords are ignored until a new game.
- The player can end a game early only by starting a new one; there is no resign or draw.
- The board is not resized or changed mid-game.

action_protocol_block:
The rules the product enforces (plan the audience's side of them; the business's own back-office handling is out of view):
- [New game starts in ready state] (Game): Given a player chooses a difficulty When a new game is created Then the game is in the ready state with elapsed seconds 0 and no tile revealed
- [Difficulty sizes] (Game): Given a difficulty is chosen When the game is created Then its board and mine count match the Beginner 9x9/10, Intermediate 16x16/40 or Expert 30x16/99 preset, and no other size is accepted
- [First reveal places mines safely] (Game): Given a ready game When the player reveals a hidden tile Then mines are placed excluding that tile and its adjacent neighbours
- [First reveal starts game and timer] (Game): Given a ready game When the first reveal occurs Then the game status becomes in progress and started_at is recorded
- [Flagging before first reveal allowed without timer] (Game): Given a ready game When the player flags a hidden tile Then the flag is placed and the game remains in the ready state with no started_at
- [Adjacent mine count] (Game): Given a generated board When counts are computed Then each tile's adjacent_mine_count equals the number of mines among its neighbours within 0 to 8
- [Reveal a safe hidden tile] (Game): Given an in-progress game and a hidden safe tile When the player reveals it Then the tile state becomes revealed
- [Revealing a mine loses the game] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the player reveals a mine Then the game status becomes lost and ended_at is recorded
- [Revealing all safe tiles wins] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the last non-mine tile is revealed without flagging mines Then the game status becomes won and the timer stops
- [Zero tile cascade] (Game): Given an in-progress game When a zero tile is revealed Then all its neighbours are revealed and any zero neighbours cascade further
- [Cascade skips flags and stops at numbers] (Game): Given a cascade from a zero tile When it reaches a flagged tile Then the flagged tile stays flagged and When it reaches a numbered tile Then the cascade does not continue through it
- [Revealing a flagged tile refused] (Game): Given an in-progress game and a flagged tile When the player reveals it Then the tile remains flagged and the game state is unchanged
- [Place and remove flags on hidden tiles] (Game): Given an in-progress game When the player flags a hidden tile Then it becomes flagged; When the player flags a flagged tile Then the flag is removed; When the player flags a revealed tile Then nothing changes
- [Flag count may exceed mines] (Game): Given a game with 10 mines and 12 flags placed Then flag_count is 12 and the counter value is -2
- [Chord reveals neighbours when flags match] (Game): Given a revealed number tile whose adjacent flag count equals its number When the player chords it Then all other unflagged hidden neighbours are revealed
- [Chord ignored when flags mismatch] (Game): Given a revealed number tile whose adjacent flag count differs from its number When the player chords it Then no tile changes
- [Wrong flag chord can lose] (Game): Given a number tile with a wrongly placed flag and matching flag count When the player chords it Then the unflagged mine is revealed and the game is lost
- [Chord on zero tile does nothing] (Game): Given a hidden or revealed zero tile When the player chords it Then no tile changes
- [Timer ticks and stops at end] (Game): Given an in-progress game When one second passes Then elapsed_seconds increases by 1 up to 999; When the game is won or lost Then elapsed_seconds stops changing
- [Actions ignored after game ends] (Game): Given a won or lost game When the player reveals, flags or chords any tile Then the game state is unchanged
- [Win reveals mines as flags] (Game): Given a game is won Then every unflagged mine tile becomes flagged and the mine counter displays 000
- [Loss reveals mines and wrong flags] (Game): Given a game is lost Then all unflagged mines are revealed, the clicked mine is marked exploded, and each wrongly flagged non-mine is marked as a wrong flag
- [New game keeps difficulty or changes it] (Game): Given a game in any state When the face button is pressed Then a new ready game with the same difficulty is created; When a different difficulty is chosen Then a new ready game at that size is created; Given an in-progress game Then its board size does not change
- [No resign or draw] (Game): Given an in-progress game Then the only outcomes are won or lost, and ending early occurs only by creating a new game
- [Face button shows shocked state while pressing] (Game): Given a tile is pressed and held When the press is active Then the face displays the shocked state; Given a game is won Then the face displays sunglasses; Given a game is lost Then the face displays dead eyes
- [Hidden and revealed tile visuals] (Game): Given a tile is hidden Then it is displayed as a raised grey square; Given a tile is revealed with count n Then it is displayed flat with the colour for n, and blank when n is 0
intent_block:
- Product type: game
- Audience: players who want to play minesweeper for fun
- Goal: Let a player play a classic minesweeper round with clear rules, reveal and flag mechanics, and a win or loss outcome.
- Scope: A single-player minesweeper game consisting of a grid board, mine placement, cell reveal and flag interactions, and game state tracking through win or loss.
- The model must cover: board grid and cell state (hidden, revealed, flagged); mine layout and adjacency counts; game session state and outcome (in progress, won, lost); player moves (reveal, flag)
- Do NOT model: user accounts and login; leaderboards or online multiplayer; payments or monetisation; admin or back-office management of games
